source_excerpts.text:
AN ELEMENTARY ODD-DEGREE ENDPOINT LEMMA

Lemma. Let p(z)=a_0+a_1 z+...+a_d z^d be a real polynomial of odd degree d with
a_0,a_d>0 and no zero in Re z>0. Then

                       a_0 a_d <= a_1 a_(d-1).                       (L)

Proof. All its roots rho_i satisfy Re rho_i<=0; none is zero because a_0>0.
Put r_i=-1/rho_i. Then Re r_i>=0 and

 p(z)=a_0 product_i (1+r_i z),
 a_1/a_0=sum_i r_i,
 a_(d-1)/a_d=sum_i 1/r_i.

The nonreal r_i occur in conjugate pairs. Each such pair contributes
2 Re r_i>=0 to the first sum and 2 Re(1/r_i)>=0 to the second. Since d is odd,
at least one r_i is real. Every real r_i is strictly positive: rho_i is real,
nonzero, and in the closed left half-plane. Let R be the nonempty multiset of
these positive real r_i. Hence

 (a_1/a_0)(a_(d-1)/a_d)
 >= (sum_{r in R} r)(sum_{r in R}1/r)
 >= |R|^2 >= 1,

where the second inequality is Cauchy-Schwarz. This proves (L). Multiplicities
and imaginary-axis roots cause no difficulty. There is no strict-stability
perturbation assumption. For d=1 the assertion is equality.

The odd-degree hypothesis is essential: p(z)=1+z^2 has no root in Re z>0 but
has a_0 a_2=1 and a_1^2=0. The lemma needs no sign assumption on the middle
coefficients; their nonnegativity in the application is independently available.

This is the entire univariate ingredient. Asner's total-nonnegativity theorem
for Hurwitz matrices also implies this endpoint minor inequality, but that
stronger imported theorem and the alternative Pick-residue argument are not
required here.

DEPENDENCIES / PRIMARY SOURCE COMPARISON

1. Elementary polynomial factorization over the complex numbers,
   conjugation of roots of a real polynomial, and Cauchy-Schwarz.
2. Boundary specialization of a stable polynomial is stable or zero. A primary
   reference is Petter Branden, Polynomials with the half-plane property and
   matroid theory (2007), Proposition 2.2(2) and Theorem 2.3 (Hurwitz):
   https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0607755
   Local text: work/cycle3/canonical_bcs_sources/math_0607755.txt, around lines
   193-214. Rotation transfers this statement between upper and right
   half-planes; inversion and positive diagonal substitutions were checked
   directly above.
3. Related stronger classical result: B. A. Asner, Jr., On the Total
   Nonnegativity of the Hurwitz Matrix, SIAM Journal on Applied Mathematics
   18(2), 407-414 (1970), https://doi.org/10.1137/0118035. Publisher metadata
   and the later primary paper below were read; the paywalled original full
   proof was not imported. Our root proof avoids relying on it.
4. Mohammad Adm, Jurgen Garloff, Mikhail Tyaglov, Total nonnegativity of finite
   Hurwitz matrices and root location of polynomials (2017/2018),
   https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.04651, primary full text
   https://d-nb.info/1147681783/34. It states the closed-left-half-plane to
   finite-Hurwitz-total-nonnegativity implication and revisits Asner's theorem.
5. Nima Anari, Kuikui Liu, Shayan Oveis Gharan, Cynthia Vinzant, Thuy-Duong
   Vuong, Log-Concave Polynomials IV: Approximate Exchange, Tight Mixing
   Times, and Near-Optimal Sampling of Forests, arXiv:2004.07220v2 (2021),
   https://arxiv.org/html/2004.07220v2, Lemmas 26 and 28, full proof read.
   Lemma 26 proves square-root exchange for fixed-size nonnegative real-stable
   coefficients. Its proof builds an odd-degree Hurwitz polynomial and balances
   fields. Lemma 28 is precisely the endpoint inequality (L), derived there
   from Asner. Thus (L) and the general exchange mechanism are established
   prior art. The audited extension uses full reciprocal twists and constant
   parity to cover nonhomogeneous right-half-plane-stable coefficients. The
   elementary root proof here is an alternative proof, not a new inequality.
